scenes.vo: In twenty fourteen, a private equity firm bought Red Lobster — then sold the real estate out from under it.

visual.sub:
GOLDEN GATE CAPITAL BOUGHT
RED LOBSTER FROM DARDEN

scenes.vo: To fund the deal, the buyer sold the land and buildings under about five hundred locations for one point five billion — then leased them back to Red Lobster.

items.text: Real estate under ~500 stores sold for $1.5B
Red Lobster then rented buildings it used to own

scenes.vo: Those leases climbed about two percent every year — and the year before bankruptcy, rent alone cost Red Lobster over one hundred ninety million dollars.

visual.sub:
SPENT ON RENT ALONE —
ON BUILDINGS IT USED TO OWN

scenes.vo: Everyone blamed the twenty dollar Endless Shrimp deal. It lost eleven million dollars in one quarter — but it wasn't the real problem.

visual.sub:
LOST $11M IN ONE QUARTER —
BUT WASN'T THE REAL PROBLEM

scenes.vo: Red Lobster's bankruptcy filing points to the lease payments from that deal as the weight that sank the chain.

visual.sub:
THE 2014 SALE-LEASEBACK — NOT
THE SHRIMP — SANK THE CHAIN

scenes.vo: Red Lobster filed for Chapter Eleven in May twenty twenty four, then exited bankruptcy under a new owner that fall.
When private equity sells the ground out from under a company it just bought, the rent bill — not the menu — decides if it survives.

visual.display: When private equity sells the *ground* out from under a company it just bought, the *rent* *bill* — not the menu — decides if it *survives.*
